doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Selfish enlightenment and goodbyes
summary: She adds that living for yourself is a gift, offers get a puppy and follow your heart, and they say goodbye.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I’ll just pause this and we’ll say our good-byes.
Okay. I had one other thing.

You know yes, I wanted to say yes that happiness – my happiness does come from helping others that are suffering but I have also learned and this never would have happened had I not been relieved of my 17-hour days from this crazy job in this crazy foundation that I built. But I want to say that what I learned was that when you live for yourself, when you give to yourself, when you make time to live your life in a way that makes you happy, just the way the musicians did, and the way I did all these years, but

there is another level. There is another layer to the onion when you peel. And the glorious selfish enlightenment is a gift. It’s okay to do for yourself. We live in a society where the noble people who give their life to service, there is nothing wrong with living your life selfishly and in a way that makes you happy and doing, choosing things that make you happy. And I say this because if everyone in this world lived according to their heart and according to doing what makes you happy there would be no war. Who would want to give up that life? Who would be so miserable from resentment that they have to be violent, that they have to be angry? They’d be too happy. So like the way I see it is get a puppy and follow your heart. And there will be peace in the world so there’s my optimism. Okay? For this moment in the world.
That was a beautiful coda to our conversation, and a wonderful quote.
Much love, Monk, you’re an amazing guy and thank you, thank you for what you do.
And thanks for this opportunity. Bye.
